comment: The revert-checks of the state-write path its callers depend on (#181, #188, #182): one mutation per invariant, the named case must go red, the file is restored, the case must go green again. Run it with `bash tools/mutate.sh --mutations tools/close-mutations.json`; `.pi/skills/mutation-runner` owns how, `.pi/skills/revert-check` owns the rule, and the CI step that owns the issue tooling prints `--list`, so a set that no longer parses fails the pipeline instead of rotting. Every search is a single line and unique in its file (the runner's replacement is literal and line-based). The fourth entry mutates the profile reader into a silent fallback rather than a refusal: a mutation that removes the guard line would leave a bare string as a command, which is a syntax accident rather than the invariant under test.

mutations.label: A1.1
mutations.why: the settled state being written before the closure — without it an item is closed and still reads on-hold

mutations.label: A1.2
mutations.why: a person's not-planned decision recording the state a fix records

mutations.label: A1.3
mutations.search: gh "${args[@]}" || issues_die "update: gh could not write #$number's labels — nothing was recorded"
mutations.why: a rejected label write exiting 0, so the caller proceeds from a state the tracker does not carry

mutations.label: A1.4
mutations.why: a half-adapted profile being refused instead of silently recording the fix state

mutations.label: A1.5
mutations.why: the `already carries` note being printed only by a call that named a state (#182)
